turns.content: Let the positive integer side lengths of the three non-overlapping axis-parallel squares be a, b, and c. Each square has a vertex at the origin, and their union has area 41. Write the Diophantine equation that the side lengths must satisfy.
Enumerate all positive integer triples satisfying that area equation, up to permutation, and justify that the list is complete.

Suppose the square of side x lies between squares of side x and y around the origin. Trace the exposed boundary in order and express the union perimeter using absolute differences among the stated side lengths.
Rewrite the perimeter formula using min(m,x) and min(m,y), and explain how the two overlaps reduce the sum of the three individual perimeters.
For a fixed triple of side lengths, compare the three possible choices of the middle square and determine which choice maximizes the union perimeter.
Apply that placement rule to every admissible triple and determine the largest possible perimeter.
